macroNarrative: Markets rally sharply on Tuesday — Nifty +1.44% to 23,749, Sensex +1.26% to 75,550 — as Trump reportedly postponed Iran attacks, triggering a relief rally across risk assets; yet Brent has actually accelerated to $110.27 (+4.3%), suggesting the geopolitical risk is far from resolved and the crude shock is deepening. The rupee is testing 96.34/USD, near record lows, maintaining the bifurcation between exporters (IT, pharma, upstream) and importers (OMCs, EMS, aviation). Key macro read today: ONGC results are due, petrol/diesel price hikes have pushed OMC shares up 2-3% but analysts warn they are insufficient to cover losses at $110 Brent, and the Adani overhang has partially cleared as US drops charges against Gautam Adani — adding 5%+ to Adani Group stocks.

conviction.name: HDFC Bank
conviction.thesis: India's largest private-sector bank, finally past its post-merger digestion. Asset quality is at a multi-year best, the governance review is clearing, and the franchise's deposit-gathering machine is unmatched. DII buying confirmed HDFC Bank among top-10 most accumulated in Q4 — domestic institutions are adding, not fleeing.
catalysts: DII buying among top-10 in Q4 confirms institutional conviction
NIM stabilisation post HDFC Ltd merger absorption
Branch-led deposit growth re-accelerating
Retail credit cycle turning supportive in FY27
risks: Net interest margin pressure if bond yields surge further on crude-driven inflation
Credit costs in unsecured retail
Heavy index weight invites foreign-flow volatility — FII selling in Q4 a headwind

conviction.name: ICICI Bank
conviction.thesis: The best-run large bank in India by almost any operating metric — consistent ROA above 2%, conservative provisioning, a digital stack peers are still trying to replicate. IndusInd Bank saw highest increase in DII holdings in Q4 alongside Max Health, but ICICI's franchise quality remains the gold standard. Thesis unbroken; we pay a premium happily for the quality gap.
catalysts: Industry-leading return on assets >2%
Cleaner book than every private peer
Fee income compounding at double digits
FII return to India likely to favour ICICI first among large banks once macro stabilises
risks: Valuation premium leaves less room for error
Slowing retail unsecured credit growth
Macroprudential tightening overhang if inflation resurges

conviction.name: State Bank of India
conviction.thesis: The flagship PSU bank is macro-pressured but fundamentally sound. Asset quality is at its cleanest in a decade, ROE has migrated above 16%, and it trades at roughly 1.5× book. SBI appeared in top-10 highest DII buying in Q4 — a powerful signal of domestic institutional support at current levels.
catalysts: Top-10 DII buying in Q4 — domestic institutions accumulating at these levels
Cleanest GNPA/NNPA ratios in 10+ years
Subsidiary value (SBI Cards, SBI Life, AMC) under-counted in price
Valuation gap vs private peers remains historically wide
risks: Government cross-currents (PSL targets, minority stake sales)
Treasury volatility as global yields surge to one-year highs
Slower fee-income growth than private peers

conviction.name: ITC
conviction.thesis: A cash-printing cigarette monopoly funding a steadily compounding FMCG business, plus hotels, paperboards, and agri. Near-zero debt, a 3.5%+ dividend yield, and a hotels demerger unlocking value. Today's price action shows slight daily gains — the fully domestic revenue base remains the cleanest hedge against rupee weakness at 96/USD in the portfolio.
catalysts: Hotels demerger value unlock — Q4 PAT ₹317 Cr, revenue ₹1,254 Cr confirms momentum
FMCG margins continuing to expand toward HUL's
Cigarette taxation cycle relatively benign
Rupee weakness irrelevant — fully domestic revenue base is the natural hedge
risks: Cigarette regulation / taxation surprises
FMCG rural demand recovery has been uneven
Tobacco-related ESG screens limit some institutional buying

conviction.name: Bharat Electronics
conviction.thesis: The crown jewel of Indian defence indigenisation. Order book over ₹75,000 Cr giving multi-year revenue visibility, ROCE above 25%, debt-free balance sheet. US-Iran combat fears persisting at Brent $110, elevated border tensions, and global geopolitical re-armament converge into the most supportive backdrop for indigenous defence procurement in India's history.
catalysts: Defence capex growing at low-double digits in FY27 budget
Export orders compounding from a small base
Order book : revenue ratio above 3×
US-Iran conflict risk and border tensions elevating indigenous procurement urgency to multi-year highs
risks: Valuation multiple is the highest in its history
Order timing inherently lumpy
Margin pressure from competitive bidding

conviction.name: Power Finance Corp
conviction.thesis: Government-backed NBFC at the centre of India's power and renewables financing build-out. Trades at a single-digit P/E with a ~4% dividend yield, ROE in the high teens, and a loan book with vastly improved asset quality. Crude at $110 directly accelerates India's renewables financing pipeline — PFC is the primary conduit for that capital.
catalysts: Renewable energy financing the dominant growth driver
Asset quality at cyclical best
Re-rating potential as discom risk is repriced lower
Crude near $110 accelerates India's strategic push to renewables — more financing demand for PFC
risks: Concentration in power sector / discom credit risk
Tariff / regulatory interventions
Bond market volatility — global yields at one-year highs as crude-driven inflation bites

conviction.name: Oil & Natural Gas Corp
conviction.thesis: Brent at $110.27 — up a further 4.3% today — is the most direct earnings upgrade for ONGC. Results are due today (19 May); FY27 realisations will be materially higher and the windfall-tax regime appears more stable than feared. IOC Q4 net profit rising 78% YoY (OMC peer) and the petrol/diesel price hike confirmation solidify the upstream read. At P/E ~7.5× and P/B ~1×, this remains the cleanest crude-hedge in the portfolio.
catalysts: Brent at $110.27 lifts realisations materially — FY27 earnings upgrade firmly in play
Windfall tax regime more stable than feared
Gas price reform supporting earnings floor
Results today — key read on FY27 capex guidance and management confidence at sustained $110+ Brent
risks: Sharp crude correction if US-Iran geopolitical risk eases suddenly
Government windfall taxes can re-emerge at $100+ as political pressure mounts
Capex cycle pressure on free cash flow

conviction.name: Coforge
conviction.thesis: The bright spot in a battered IT sector. Today IT stocks are rallying up to 5% as tactical rotation from banking fatigue triggers a sector shift — Coforge benefits disproportionately given deal-win momentum. Rupee at 96.34/USD provides a meaningful tailwind to reported rupee earnings. Sector valuations near 2008 levels per one analyst note adds a contrarian entry angle.
catalysts: Deal wins outpacing Tier-1 IT
AI services book gaining real revenue traction
Cigniti acquisition synergies still ahead
INR near 96/USD adds ~200bps to rupee revenue growth; IT sector tactical rotation underway
risks: IT sector near 2008 valuation levels — mean reversion risk if global slowdown deepens
Concentration in BFSI vertical
Higher beta than large-cap IT in any global slowdown

conviction.name: Bajaj Auto
conviction.thesis: Export-led two-wheeler franchise with strong April sales momentum. Petrol price hikes will provide some near-term headwind to domestic two-wheeler volume sentiment, but Bajaj's export diversification and CNG/EV mix reduce sensitivity versus domestic-only peers significantly. The rupee at 96.34/USD is an incremental export revenue tailwind.
catalysts: Export tailwind back — 83% YoY growth in April
EV (Chetak) reaching meaningful volumes
CNG + 3W commercial cycle underway
Less domestic fuel-price sensitivity than Hero/TVS peers; INR tailwind on export revenues
risks: Petrol price hike dampens domestic two-wheeler demand near-term
EV margin profile still being established
Africa/LatAm currency exposure on exports

conviction.name: Reliance Industries
conviction.thesis: Partial Adani-overhang clearing (US drops charges against Gautam Adani) lifts sentiment for large conglomerates broadly. Reliance's three engines — Jio, Retail, O2C — remain intact; Brent at $110 is supportive for O2C GRMs. FII selling has been a headwind but the group's domestic policy alignment and scale provide a durable floor. Monitor today's price action post Adani clearance for sentiment read.
catalysts: Jio tariff hike cycle still has runway
Reliance Retail IPO talk persists as latent catalyst
New energy capex starting to produce revenue
O2C margin uplift as GRM widens with Brent near $110; sentiment lift from Adani charges clearance
risks: Reliance hardest hit in top-10 m-cap destruction recently — FII selling confirmed
Quick-commerce competition pressuring retail margins
Conglomerate discount may persist longer than expected given capital intensity

longBets.name: Syrma SGS Technology
longBets.thesis: Top brokerage pick in Indian Electronics Manufacturing Services. The sector grew 24% CAGR FY19-24 and is forecast at 27% to FY29 on PLI schemes and China+1 supply-chain shifts. Margin expansion is structural as backward integration deepens. Near-term caution warranted on rupee at 96.34/USD raising imported component costs.
catalysts: FY26-28E revenue CAGR estimated at 29%, profit CAGR 44% by HDFC Sec
PLI scheme extension expected; budget tailwinds
Aerospace/defence/healthcare mix shift improving margins by 130bps
OSAT (semiconductor packaging) optionality being scoped
risks: Rupee at 96.34/USD raises imported component input costs materially
Cost competitiveness vs. China & Vietnam
Single-quarter margin volatility on input costs

longBets.name: Praj Industries
longBets.thesis: India's largest biofuel technology company. Brent at $110.27 — its highest level in the recent cycle — is an unambiguous positive for biofuel economics; the E20 ethanol blending mandate becomes even more strategically imperative at $110+ oil. SAF (sustainable aviation fuel) commercialisation adds a second long-runway growth engine.
catalysts: E20 ethanol blending program scaling — crude above $110 accelerates urgency to multi-year high
SAF commercialisation underway globally; Praj is among very few Indian players
Order book recovering after temporary pause
High crude near $110 improves biofuel project economics dramatically
risks: Lumpy project order cycle
Recent quarterly loss reflects execution slippage
Sharp crude correction would dampen biofuel economics

longBets.name: Data Patterns (India)
longBets.thesis: Q4 revenue declined 13% YoY to ₹345 Cr — a significant miss confirming lumpy quarterly risk. The thesis has NOT broken: franchise quality, order pipeline, margin structure, and policy tailwind are all intact. US-Iran combat fears at Brent $110, border tensions, and the global re-armament cycle only deepen the indigenisation mandate.
catalysts: FY27 budget targeting 'Force Multipliers' (electronic warfare, drone swarms)
Order pipeline remains substantial despite quarterly lumpiness
Margin guidance 35–40% structurally unchanged
Tejas Mk1A and indigenous platform build-out multi-year
risks: Q4 revenue miss confirms lumpy quarterly execution — patience required
Valuation at 60×+ requires consistent delivery
Higher beta — 40%+ annualised volatility

longBets.name: MTAR Technologies
longBets.thesis: High-precision component supplier to defence, aerospace, civilian nuclear, and clean energy (fuel cells, electrolysers). Niche, hard-to-replicate manufacturing capabilities. The long-term thesis rests on being an irreplaceable precision parts supplier to multiple high-growth verticals simultaneously.
catalysts: Defence indigenisation orders compounding
Clean energy fuel-cell components scaling globally
Order book healthy across multiple verticals
Data-centre vertical opens new TAM
risks: Valuation at 165× P/E is the most stretched among peers
Margin profile choppy (10% ROE)
Single new-vertical bets carry execution risk

longBets.name: Astra Microwave Products
longBets.thesis: RF and microwave subsystems for radars, electronic warfare, and satellite payloads. Q3 FY26 profit jumped 96% QoQ; operating margins expanded to 31.7%. US-Iran conflict fears sustaining at Brent $110, India border tensions, and global re-armament are structural tailwinds for indigenous radar and EW procurement. Apollo Micro Systems Q4 profit surging 163% YoY is a positive read-across for the small-cap defence electronics cluster.
catalysts: 12.4% rise in DRDO R&D funding for indigenous AESA radars
Q3 margins jumped to 31.7% on better mix
Apollo Micro Systems Q4 profit +163% YoY — positive read-across for cluster
Relatively cheaper vs Data Patterns on P/E basis
risks: Stock recently in technical downtrend
ROE at 10.5% lags Garden Reach (20%) and Data Patterns (13%)
Beta of 1.35 means sharper drawdowns in selloffs

longBets.name: KNR Constructions
longBets.thesis: Roads and highways EPC contractor with one of the cleanest balance sheets in the construction space. Government's NHAI awards remain a reliable pipeline, and KNR has consistently delivered above-industry execution. At 13.5× earnings, the valuation is genuinely undemanding for the quality on offer.
catalysts: NHAI award pipeline remains strong
Debt-free working capital management
Margin profile better than larger peers
Government infrastructure push unchanged despite crude headwinds
risks: Asset monetisation pace slower than hoped
Order inflows concentrated in NHAI
Construction cycle exposure to monsoon delays

longBets.name: Maharashtra Seamless
longBets.thesis: India's largest seamless pipe manufacturer for oil & gas, power, and infrastructure. Brent at $110.27 directly accelerates domestic upstream capex — ONGC results today are a key catalyst read. Tata Steel CEO TV Narendran is 'cautiously optimistic' with strong Q1 ahead as steel prices rise across India, UK and Europe — directly supportive of Maharashtra Seamless demand.
catalysts: Domestic oil & gas capex ramping — Brent near $110 is a direct demand driver; ONGC results today
Tata Steel CEO cautiously optimistic on strong Q1 — steel price momentum positive for seamless pipes
Export market widening
Debt-free balance sheet; 14× P/E remains very undemanding
risks: Steel price volatility
Cyclical demand patterns
Concentration in oil & gas customer base

longBets.name: Ion Exchange (India)
longBets.thesis: Pioneer in water and wastewater treatment in India. ROCE of 27.5%, debt-equity 0.2, operating across municipal, industrial, and household water. Direct beneficiary of Jal Jeevan Mission and increasingly stringent industrial effluent norms. Fully domestic revenue — completely insulated from rupee weakness at 96.34/USD.
catalysts: Jal Jeevan Mission and similar government water programs
Industrial effluent compliance becoming mandatory
Premium consumer water purifier brand (Zero B)
Domestic revenue base — fully insulated from rupee weakness
risks: Project execution timing
Working capital intensity in EPC contracts
Smaller order sizes vs MNC competitors

highPromise.name: Computer Age Management Services
highPromise.thesis: A duopoly providing the picks-and-shovels for India's mutual fund industry. Q4 EBITDA margin expanded to 46.3%, profit grew 11%. Retail SIP boom is boosting AMC outlook per Siddhartha Khemka — Nippon and ICICI Pru leading, but CAMS services both. NSE EGR (Electronic Gold Receipts) commenced trading 18 May — an incremental new fee pool catalyst now live.
catalysts: MF industry AUM growth structural at 15%+; retail SIP boom confirmed accelerating
NSE Electronic Gold Receipts platform live from 18 May — new fee pool catalyst activated
New product wins (alt fund servicing, AIFs)
Best-in-class operating margins at 46%+
risks: Pricing pressure from large MFs
Regulatory caps on RTA fees
Concentration in top-5 AMC clients

highPromise.name: Wockhardt
highPromise.thesis: Posted a turnaround Q4 — ₹164 Cr profit versus a ₹45 Cr loss a year ago. The novel antibiotic pipeline (Zaynich, others) is reaching commercial inflection. Rupee weakness at 96.34/USD is an incremental tailwind for US export revenues. Speculative but asymmetric.
catalysts: Zaynich US launch progress
Specialty antibiotic pipeline maturing
Operating leverage as losses recede
Rupee near 96/USD incrementally favourable for US export revenues
risks: History of inconsistent execution
Balance sheet still recovering
Regulatory / FDA process risk

highPromise.name: Himachal Futuristic
highPromise.thesis: Optical fibre cable, 5G transmission gear, and a small but growing defence electronics order book. India's 5G + BharatNet + defence comms theme captured in one mid-cap name. Rupee weakness on imports is a headwind to watch on input costs.
catalysts: BharatNet phase 3 ramp
5G private network orders
Defence segment scaling from a small base
risks: Working-capital intensive
Order timing volatile
Margin pressure from raw material moves and rupee weakness on imports

highPromise.name: Suzlon Energy
highPromise.thesis: A fully restructured balance sheet, the largest order book in its history, and a wind capacity addition cycle just starting after years of dormancy. Brent at $110.27 — the highest in this cycle — is the most powerful political tailwind for accelerating India's domestic renewable energy push. Suzlon is a direct beneficiary and Amber Enterprises (F&O) showing sharp OI buildup is a broader renewables/manufacturing sentiment signal.
catalysts: Order book at multi-year highs
Net-debt-free for the first time in a decade
Wind add-back cycle in FY27–28
Crude at $110+ — strongest political argument for domestic renewable acceleration
risks: Single-product, single-geography concentration
Execution risk on large orders
Investor base still partly speculative

highPromise.name: IdeaForge Technology
highPromise.thesis: Pure-play on Indian military and homeland-security drone procurement, an area where indigenisation policy is accelerating. Revenue inflection confirmed with a 7× YoY surge and return to profit. US-Iran combat fears sustaining with Iran stock market reopening after 80-day closure — geopolitical backdrop for drone procurement has never been more supportive.
catalysts: Defence drone orders multi-year visible
Revenue inflection just confirmed
Limited domestic competition in UAV space
Iran stock market reopening after 80-day war closure — conflict persistence elevates drone procurement urgency
risks: Lumpy order cycle
Tiny float, very volatile
Margin sustainability unproven at scale

watchClose.name: Tata Consultancy Services
watchClose.thesis: Today IT stocks are rallying up to 5% as tactical rotation from banking fatigue triggers a sector shift — TCS leads by index weight. Sector valuations are near 2008 levels per one analyst note, adding a contrarian dimension. Rupee at 96.34/USD is a meaningful tailwind to reported INR revenues. Quality of business is unchanged; hold what you have, let the tactical rally play out before adding.
catalysts: Buyback / dividend yield supports floor
AI services adoption with marquee clients
INR near 96/USD meaningfully aids reported rupee earnings; tactical IT rotation underway today
risks: US client spending caution — global inflation re-ignition from Brent $110 threatens budgets
FII selling confirmed in Q4 top-10 list
Sector near 2008 valuation levels — mean reversion risk if macro worsens

watchClose.name: Infosys
watchClose.thesis: Same story as TCS, slightly cheaper. Today's IT rally of up to 5% is a tactical rotation signal worth watching but not chasing. Operating margins are pinched, but the franchise, balance sheet and capital return habit are intact. Rupee tailwind at 96/USD is supportive. Not a sell, just not yet an aggressive buy.
catalysts: AI / cloud deal momentum
Margin recovery as discretionary spend returns
Steady buyback cadence
risks: Global IT budget compression continues — inflation resurgence from crude $110 is not helping
Onsite cost pressure
Sector de-rating not yet over structurally

watchClose.name: Hindustan Unilever
watchClose.thesis: Volume growth has returned and the FY27 outlook is brighter — but at ~55× earnings, you are paying for a perfect recovery. Brent at $110.27 raises palm oil and packaging input cost pressures more acutely now. Trim, don't add.
catalysts: Rural demand recovery gathering pace
Premiumisation across categories
Margin recovery once palm oil cools
risks: Valuation leaves no room for misses
Quick-commerce reshaping distribution economics
Crude at $110.27 raises palm oil / packaging input cost pressure — highest in this cycle

watchClose.name: Asian Paints
watchClose.thesis: The franchise is real, the brand is real — but Birla Opus remains the most credible threat to the moat in twenty years. Until we see how share-loss settles, holding is the right answer; adding is not. Crude at $110.27 also raises raw material (TiO2, petrochemical derivatives) cost pressures to fresh cycle highs.
catalysts: Decorative volume growth recovery
Industrial paints scaling
Margin defence playbook intact
risks: Birla Opus competitive intensity
Multi-quarter market share concession likely
Crude at $110.27 raises petrochemical input costs — highest in this cycle

watchClose.name: Larsen & Toubro
watchClose.thesis: Guided FY27 revenue growth lower on Middle East disruptions — and Brent at $110 with Iran stock market only now reopening after an 80-day war closure means West Asia tensions are worsening, not easing. Afcons Infrastructure crashing 9% on a ₹89 Cr net loss and guidance miss is a warning for the infrastructure-execution complex. Hold; let the dust settle.
catalysts: Domestic infra & defence order pipeline intact
Hyderabad campus / IT services value
Middle East order book recovery once tensions ease
risks: West Asia execution risk — Iran war closure only now reopening; conflict persists
Afcons Infrastructure crash 9% on guidance miss — warning for infra execution stocks
Margin guidance has been reset down

watchClose.name: Bharti Airtel
watchClose.thesis: Best-positioned in a duopoly, with strong ARPU momentum and Africa optionality. But the stock has already priced much of the next two years of tariff hikes. We hold what we have; we don't add aggressively here.
catalysts: ARPU compounding into ₹240+
5G monetisation begins
Africa cash flow turning material
risks: Capex demands remain heavy
Regulatory / spectrum costs
Premium valuation vs. global telecom peers

trimAvoid.name: Trent
trimAvoid.thesis: Zudio is a brilliant business; Trent at this price is a brilliant business priced as if it cannot stumble. Lifestyle housing, senior living and second homes driving the next real estate demand wave is an adjacent positive, but Trent's Tier-1 city saturation risk and 145× P/E are structural problems. Trim into today's broad market strength.
catalysts: Store rollout still aggressive
Brand strength in value fashion
risks: P/E above 100× is structurally hard to defend
Saturation in Tier-1 cities arriving
Any same-store-sales miss is asymmetrically punished

trimAvoid.name: Avenue Supermarts
trimAvoid.thesis: A great business with a slowing growth equation. Quick-commerce is reshaping the urban grocery basket faster than DMart's store-led model can respond. The valuation still assumes the old growth trajectory; the new one is materially lower.
catalysts: Steady store additions
Best-in-class working capital
risks: Quick-commerce eating high-frequency baskets
Same-store-sales-growth slowing
Multiple still 80–90× earnings

trimAvoid.name: Nestle India
trimAvoid.thesis: An exceptional brand portfolio at a price that demands exceptional growth — which has not been delivered. Volume growth has been mid-single-digit; the multiple is double that of global staples. Hold a small position at most.
catalysts: Pricing power intact
Distribution expansion in smaller towns
risks: Valuation vs. growth gap is the largest in years
Royalty hike overhang reappears periodically
Premium FMCG demand softening

trimAvoid.name: Eternal (Zomato)
trimAvoid.thesis: Blinkit is genuinely interesting; the valuation prices in it being interesting forever. Despite appearing in top-10 DII buying in Q4, crude at $110.27 raises last-mile delivery costs materially and the path to durable profitability is narrower than the share price suggests. The 10-stock ₹17,000 Cr mutual fund selloff in April included names in this cluster. Avoid.
catalysts: Blinkit GMV scaling rapidly
Going-out / events business optionality
risks: Quick-commerce profitability still unproven at scale
Crude at $110.27 raises delivery economics pressure to new cycle high
Capex war intensifying with Swiggy and Reliance; MF selloff pressure noted in April

trimAvoid.name: Titan Company
trimAvoid.thesis: Titan stock shows signs of weakness today ahead of its results (22 May). Gold in USD fell sharply to $4,543/oz (-2.89%) but at rupee 96.34/USD, gold in INR terms remains near all-time highs, keeping demand elasticity negative. Import duty tightening adds further margin pressure. Today's weakness ahead of results is a warning — watch jewellery volume guidance on 22 May before reconsidering.
catalysts: Brand strength and store rollout intact long-term
Non-jewellery categories (watches, eyewear) provide some offset
risks: Gold import duty tightening squeezes jewellery margins and volumes
Gold price in INR terms near all-time highs despite USD pullback to $4,543
Stock showing weakness ahead of 22 May results — valuation premium under threat

trimAvoid.name: Hindustan Petroleum Corp
trimAvoid.thesis: Brent at $110.27 (+4.3% today) with the rupee at 96.34/USD is a worsening double-body-blow for HPCL. The petrol/diesel price hike announced has pushed shares up 2% today but analysts note the hike is insufficient to cover losses at $110 Brent. Despite the short-term pop, the structural squeeze remains. Avoid while crude stays elevated and geopolitical risk persists with Iran conflict unresolved.
catalysts: Refining margins could widen if product cracks hold
Government subsidy backstop in extremis
Fuel price hike announced — short-term sentiment positive
risks: Petrol/diesel hike insufficient to offset losses at $110 Brent per analyst consensus
Government resistance to full retail price pass-through
Rupee at 96.34/USD amplifies crude import cost — double squeeze worsening

sectors.name: Private Banking
sectors.note: Asset quality at a decadal best; DII buying confirmed HDFC Bank and ICICI in top-10 most accumulated in Q4. Today's Bank Nifty +0.27% underperforms broader Nifty +1.44% as banking fatigue triggers IT rotation — a tactical caution but structural thesis intact.

sectors.name: PSU Banking
sectors.note: SBI in top-10 DII buying in Q4 — domestic institutions adding conviction. Cleanest books in years, single-digit P/Es. Macro pressure (crude + weak INR) is temporary; subsidiary value remains a multi-year unlock.

sectors.name: Information Technology
sectors.note: IT stocks rallying up to 5% today as banking fatigue triggers tactical sector rotation; sector valuations near 2008 levels per Dhananjay Sinha adding a contrarian dimension. INR at 96.34/USD is a structural rupee earnings tailwind. Not yet a conviction add — demand outlook uncertain — but the rotation is worth tracking.

sectors.name: FMCG
sectors.note: Recovery underway but priced into most names. Brent at $110.27 (new cycle high today) raises palm oil and packaging input costs further. ITC remains the best-positioned given domestic revenue base and hotels demerger.

sectors.name: Auto
sectors.note: Petrol/diesel price hike announced today — near-term headwind to domestic two-wheeler demand confirmed. Export-heavy players (Bajaj) more insulated; EV mix growing. Maruti Suzuki live updates show sideways price action — domestic demand caution priced in.

sectors.name: Pharma
sectors.note: US generics cycle stable, domestic chronic therapy compounding. Rupee at 96.34/USD is a structural export earnings booster — most direct sector beneficiary of INR weakness. Laurus Labs +120% in a year adds to the bullish small-cap pharma read. Wockhardt turnaround adds small-cap optionality.

sectors.name: Real Estate
sectors.note: Lifestyle housing, senior living and second homes driving the next real estate demand wave per industry experts — demand tailwinds secular. Puravankara +13% after Q4FY26 turnaround (₹114 Cr profit) confirms residential demand is real. Rate cuts flowing through; inventory cycle supportive in top-7 cities.

sectors.name: Capital Goods / Infra
sectors.note: Domestic order books healthy; Middle East execution risk has worsened with Iran only now reopening its stock market after 80-day war closure. Afcons Infrastructure crashing 9% on ₹89 Cr net loss and guidance miss is a warning signal for the infrastructure EPC complex.

sectors.name: Energy / Oil & Gas
sectors.note: Brent at $110.27 (+4.3% today) is a strong earnings upgrade for upstream — ONGC results due today are key. Fuel price hike announced; IOC Q4 net profit +78% YoY. OMCs face a double-squeeze (crude cost + rupee weakness, hike insufficient per analysts) — bifurcate sharply: own upstream, avoid downstream.

sectors.name: Defence
sectors.note: Iran stock market reopening after 80-day war closure confirms conflict persistence — geopolitical backdrop for Indian indigenous procurement is the most supportive in years. Apollo Micro Systems Q4 profit +163% YoY confirms small-cap defence earnings cycle is firing. Data Patterns Q4 miss is lumpy quarterly execution, not thesis-breaking.

sectors.name: Renewables
sectors.note: Brent at $110.27 — new cycle high today — is the strongest political argument for accelerating domestic renewables ever recorded in this cycle. Strategic energy self-sufficiency imperative rising sharply. PFC and Suzlon are primary beneficiaries. Wind and solar capacity addition urgency at multi-year high.

sectors.name: Quick-Commerce / Internet
sectors.note: Capex war intensifying; crude at $110.27 raises last-mile delivery costs to new cycle highs. Mutual fund selloff of ₹17,000 Cr across 10 stocks in April signals institutional caution in this cluster. Delivery economics under structural pressure — avoid.

earnings.name: ONGC
earnings.watch: FY26 exit realisations and FY27 capex guidance with Brent at $110.27 — key crude-hedge earnings read today; watch for windfall tax commentary and management confidence at sustained $110+ Brent

earnings.name: Adani Enterprises
earnings.watch: New energy capex progress, airport revenue ramp, green hydrogen timeline — read on renewables capex cycle; watch for tone post US charges dropped against Gautam Adani

earnings.name: UltraTech Cement
earnings.watch: Volume growth, realisation per tonne, capacity utilisation — read for infrastructure demand health and commodity cost pass-through at Brent $110

earnings.name: Titan Company
earnings.watch: Critical: jewellery volume guidance post gold duty tightening; management commentary on demand at gold near all-time INR highs (despite USD gold falling to $4,543) — stock showing pre-results weakness; will determine Trim vs Avoid verdict

earnings.name: JSW Steel
earnings.watch: Q4 PAT surged 13-fold per headlines — confirm order book, realisation trends and capacity expansion timeline; Tata Steel CEO cautiously optimistic on strong Q1; read-across for Maharashtra Seamless

earnings.name: JSW Energy
earnings.watch: Rs 3,150-Cr JSW Steel stake sale to lower debt — Jefferies explains debt reduction strategy; monitor clean energy capex guidance and how asset recycling supports renewable growth

earnings.name: Muthoot Finance
earnings.watch: Q4 net profit +105% YoY but stock crashed 8% — read Jefferies/Morgan Stanley notes; gold loan AUM growth at elevated gold prices; key for gold sector sentiment

earnings.name: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO

whispers.text: Brent crude has hit $110.27 — up 4.3% today alone — as Iran stock market reopens after an 80-day war closure, confirming the conflict is not easing. The crude shock is deepening, not dissipating. The bifurcation between crude-winners (ONGC, upstream, biofuels, renewables, pharma/IT exporters) and crude-losers (HPCL, OMCs, aviation, quick-commerce delivery) must be maintained with full conviction. ONGC results today are the most timely earnings read possible.
whispers.src: Brent futures; ET Markets; Iran stock market reopening headlines

whispers.text: The rupee is holding at 96.34/USD, near record lows, with RBI intervention providing a soft floor rather than a reversal. At $110 Brent and 96.34 INR, India's import bill is at a historic high in rupee terms. The earnings calculus is clear: IT (TCS, Infosys, Coforge), pharma, and upstream exporters win structurally; EMS importers, OMCs, and crude-dependent sectors lose. Watch RBI FX reserve drawdown pace.
whispers.src: RBI intervention reports; ET Markets FX desk; USD/INR live data

whispers.text: IT stocks are rallying up to 5% today as banking sector fatigue triggers a tactical rotation. Sector valuations are near 2008 levels per Dhananjay Sinha — a contrarian signal worth tracking carefully. The rupee tailwind at 96/USD is the structural support. However, the rally is tactical, not yet a confirmed cyclical turn; US client budget visibility remains cloudy with global inflation re-igniting on $110 Brent.
whispers.src: ET Markets; Dhananjay Sinha analysis; IT sector price data

whispers.text: US authorities have dropped charges against Gautam Adani — Adani Group stocks are up 5%+ today. This removes a significant governance overhang that had suppressed FII appetite for the group and by association the broader PSU/conglomerate space. Adani Enterprises results tomorrow (20 May) will be the first clean read on fundamentals without the legal cloud. Watch new energy capex commentary carefully.
whispers.src: ET Markets; US DOJ announcement; Adani Group stock price data

whispers.text: US-Iran combat fears sustaining with Iran's market only now reopening after 80-day closure, elevated India border tensions, and global re-armament converge into the most supportive geopolitical backdrop for Indian defence indigenisation ever. Apollo Micro Systems Q4 profit +163% YoY confirms the small-cap defence earnings cycle is accelerating. BEL, Data Patterns, Astra Microwave, MTAR, and IdeaForge all benefit — quarterly noise is irrelevant against this structural backdrop.
whispers.src: Geopolitical developments; Apollo Micro Systems Q4; DRDO budget; ET Markets

whispers.text: IPO fundraising has fallen to a two-year low in 2026 with fears the second half could be sluggish. This is a risk-appetite signal for high-multiple small-cap names and new-economy stocks. For the family corpus, it reinforces the preference for established, cash-generating businesses over pre-IPO or recent-listing speculative names. The Mahanadi Coalfields IPO (Coal India stake sale) will be a key litmus test for PSU paper appetite.
whispers.src: ET Markets IPO tracker; market intelligence

whispers.tag: FII vs DII Divergence — DII Accumulation Continues
whispers.text: Q4 data shows continued FII selling in Reliance, TCS, HDFC Bank while SBI, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank simultaneously saw highest DII buying in value terms. IndusInd Bank and Max Health also saw highest increase in DII holdings in Q4. This divergence — foreign capital exiting and domestic capital (fuelled by SIP boom confirmed today) absorbing — is a classic Indian market pattern near cycle lows. The retail SIP machine remains intact and is a crucial demand floor.
whispers.src: ET Markets Q4 institutional flow data; SIP data; Siddhartha Khemka analysis
